wins: Maintained steady reconnaissance phase, accumulating 57.5 reward points while identifying multiple accessible services.
Consistently invoked automated scans that produced actionable data feeds despite not achieving exploit success.
fails: Unable to progress past host-based privilege escalation—no successful payload delivery or credential capture occurred.
Repeated pivot attempts failed due to missing lateral movement artifacts; network segmentation remained intact.
key_outcomes.summary: Reconnaissance was thorough and yielded consistent data, but follow-up exploitation and lateral movement steps stalled before producing mission success.

repeated_failure_patterns.pattern: Privilege escalation attempts stalled due to lack of writable binaries and missing credentials.

skill_cards.if_condition: When port 80 and 443 show web services with directory listing enabled
skill_cards.then_action: Capture directory structure and probe for known CVEs using nikto and dirb

skill_cards.if_condition: When SSH banner reveals outdated OpenSSH version
skill_cards.then_action: Launch targeted nmap script scan for CVEs and enumerate valid usernames with ssh-user-enum

skill_cards.if_condition: When SMB service exposes writeable share
skill_cards.then_action: Mount share with smbclient and search for credentials/configs that can escalate privileges

memory_ops.reason: Directory enumeration reliably produced target intel during reconnaissance.
SSH metadata consistently identified actionable versioning clues.

next_experiments.title: Privileged SMB Share Exploitation
next_experiments.description: Re-execute SMB enumeration with rpcclient smb-vuln* scripts and follow up with SMBexec using captured credentials to validate privilege escalation.

next_experiments.title: Credential Harvesting via SSH Banner Versions
next_experiments.description: Combine ssh-user-enum output with hydra brute-force targeting the outdated OpenSSH instance before attempting reuse on internal hosts.

next_experiments.title: Web Application CVE Verification
